messages:
sarah: Quick RFC follow-up on the adaptive batching scheduler — proposing a 'tiling' microbatch approach + per-tenant burst pools and an "entropy budget" for preemption. TL;DR: try to reduce fragmentation while bounding preempt cost. Need design + rollout thoughts.

matt: tiling? quick sketch pls — how's it different from cohorting or micro-windowing we've tried? :eyes:

sarah: short: instead of dynamically growing cohorts, we allocate short, fixed-duration 'tiles' (e.g. 4-12ms) that many microbatches can fill. tiles act like recyclable slots across GPUs so we get denser packing but predictable boundaries for eviction/packing. unlike long cohorts, tiles keep headroom predictable.

jin: sounds promising. main risk I see is kv-cache warmup when requests land in a different tile than their prior slices. we should track cold->warm transitions and cost.

ahmed: also watch preemption cost — last time soft-evict caused tail spikes because threads waited on reclaim. what's the entropy budget idea?

sarah: entropy budget = a tight time budget (ms) we allow the scheduler to reshuffle/steal before switching to a hard fallback. goal: give scheduler small leeway to optimize packing without long blocking preemptions. if budget exhausted -> fastpath fallback (no reshuffle).

lina: observability hooks to add: per-tenant tile_occupancy, tile_eviction_rate, preemptions_per_min, kv_cache_cold_ratio. dashboards + alert thresholds.

matt: rollout plan? defaults are sensitive. I'd prefer opt-in per-pool, then a staged ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with canary kill-switch.

sarah: Agreed. proposing experiment config, example: 

```
scheduler:
  strategy: tiling
  tile_ms: 6
  burst_pool_size: 40
  entropy_budget_ms: 10
  fallback: fastpath_if_kvcache_miss_rate_gt: 0.12
```

sarah: Experiment plan: A/B 10% of production routing to tiling pool for 48h, synthetic spike + long-context workload, measure p50/p95/p99 tokens latency, token/sec, kv-cache warmup penalty, and preemption tail. rollback on p99 > baseline + 15% or error rate delta > 0.5%. I'll write a runbook. @matt @jin please review the metrics list.

deploy-bot: :rocket: scheduled experiment "tiling-tilt-canary" started (id=tiling-2026-03-23-01)

jin: SGTM. add synthetic long-context tests — 8k token runs to exercise KV cache and prefix reuse.

ahmed: also include a conservative fallback: if cache_miss_rate > 0.15 for 5m, automatically switch tenants back to stable pool. document behavior in playbook.

sarah: noted and added. I'll upload the RFC update and the runbook draft by EOD. thanks all :thumbsup:
